criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission and need well described with refs. Single-sat rationale given. Operator vs customers not distinguished; operated from Australia facilities vague. Missing clear operator/customer identification.

evidence.quote: allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All sub-sections covered with STK screenshots and access table. Multiple technical errors: inclination 87.79 not SSO, sma 7171km wrong, Kourou latitude 45.05N, contact duration misread, RAAN logic flawed. No STK files evidenced.

evidence.quote: launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport
an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 87.7924°

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Summarises launch, orbit, ground station and benefit. Largely restates design with caveat on Vega E. Lacks detailed evidence-based conclusions or quantified performance.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings, exec summary, readable writing. Figures have minimal captions, inconsistent numbering. References use bare URLs and include Wikipedia which brief forbids. Formatting inconsistent.

technical_issues.issue: SSO inclination at 600km quoted as 87.79 deg; correct ~97.8 deg as per own plot. 87.79 deg is prograde and not sun-synchronous.
Kourou latitude quoted as 45.05 deg N; actual ~5.2 deg N. Invalidates two-windows-per-day argument detail.
Mean access 580.786s (~9.7 min) described as almost twenty minutes; misinterpretation by factor 2.
RAAN 27.33 deg claimed to indicate launch facility location; RAAN does not equal launch longitude and explanation of J2 precession incomplete.

overall: Single-sat reef monitor concept well motivated. Design covers all segments with STK evidence but contains significant orbital-mechanics numerical errors and weak referencing.

feedback.summary: Your single-satellite reef-monitor concept is well motivated and you covered all mission segments with STK evidence. To reach Accomplished you need to correct key orbital-mechanics numbers, sharpen operator/customer definition and conclusions, and improve referencing and figure presentation.
next_steps: Recalculate and verify your orbit numbers in Orbit (inclination ~97.8 deg, sma 6971 km) and Kourou latitude and access-duration interpretation before finalising.
Clearly separate operator versus customers in Introduction and link each to Australia benefit with literature references.
Upgrade Conclusion to quantified evidence-based claims and fix Bibliography to full citations without Wikipedia plus consistent figure captions.

criteria.C1: You described your primary reef-monitoring mission and need well and justified one satellite in Introduction. For Accomplished, explicitly name operator versus customers and how each uses data from Australian facilities.
criteria.C2: You covered launch from Guiana, 600km orbit, manoeuvres and ground contacts with STK screenshots in Mission Design and Orbit. For Accomplished, fix inclination to SSO, sma, Kourou latitude, 580s access and RAAN logic, and include STK files.
criteria.C3: You summarised launch, orbit and ground station benefit in Conclusion. For Accomplished, draw detailed conclusions directly from your evidence with quantified performance rather than restating design.
criteria.C4: Your headings, executive summary and writing are clear and readable. For Accomplished, add informative captions and consistent numbering, and use proper full references instead of bare URLs and Wikipedia.
